parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Method 1 — ordered probabilities
$\frac5{12}\frac4{11}\frac3{10}=\frac{60}{1320},\quad \frac4{12}\frac3{11}\frac2{10}=\frac{24}{1320},\quad \frac3{12}\frac2{11}\frac1{10}=\frac6{1320}$ [M1]
Guidance: Show denominator $12\times11\times10$ or a numerator of form $a(a-1)(a-2)$ for at least one of $a=5,4,3$.
$\frac{60}{1320},\ \frac{24}{1320},\ \frac6{1320}$ [A1]
Guidance: Give one correct ordered expression $a/12\times(a-1)/11\times(a-2)/10$ for $a=5,4,3$; numerator values must be in descending order.
$\frac{60+24+6}{1320}$ [M1]
Guidance: Add all three same-colour ordered probabilities. Accept the equivalent sum $1/22+1/55+1/220$.
$\frac3{44}=0.0682$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $3/44$ or $0.0682$, dependent only on the preceding complete-sum method.
Method 2 — combinations
$\frac{\binom53}{\binom{12}3},\quad\frac{\binom43}{\binom{12}3},\quad\frac{\binom33}{\binom{12}3}$ [M1]
Guidance: Show denominator $\binom{12}{3}$ or numerator $\binom a3$ for at least one of $a=5,4,3$.
$\frac1{22},\ \frac1{55},\ \frac1{220}$ [A1]
Guidance: Give one correct expression $\binom a3/\binom{12}3$ for $a=5,4,3$.
$\frac{\binom53+\binom43+\binom33}{\binom{12}3}$ [M1]
Guidance: Add all three combination probabilities. Accept the equivalent sum $1/22+1/55+1/220$.
$\frac3{44}=0.0682$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $3/44$ or $0.0682$, dependent only on the preceding complete-sum method.
Total: 4

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$P(YYY\mid\text{all same})=\frac{60/1320}{90/1320}$ [M1]
Guidance: Use $P(YYY)$ as $60/1320$ or $1/22$, divided by the candidate’s same-colour result from part (a), such as $90/1320$ or $3/44$.
$P(YYY\mid\text{all same})=\frac23=0.667$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $2/3$ or $0.667$, or an equivalent form.
Total: 2

parts.label: (c)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Method 1 — complement
$P(\text{no orange})=\frac8{12}\frac7{11}\frac6{10}=\frac{14}{55}$ [B1]
Guidance: Show $P(\text{no orange})=(8/12)(7/11)(6/10)$ or $\binom83/\binom{12}3$. The isolated ratios $336/1320$ or $56/220$ are condoned, but not an unsupported equivalent probability.
$P(\text{at least one orange})=1-\frac{14}{55}$ [M1]
Guidance: Subtract the complete no-orange probability from one. Condone $1-14/55$ or an equivalent form, but not an unsupported $41/55$.
$\frac{41}{55}=0.745$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $41/55$ or a decimal from $0.745$ inclusive to $0.74545$ inclusive; if the method mark is not earned, special-case B1 is available for an accepted final value.
Method 2 — enumerate orange counts
$P(1O)=\frac{672}{1320},\quad P(2O)=\frac{288}{1320},\quad P(3O)=\frac{24}{1320}$ [B1]
Guidance: Give a correct probability for exactly one or exactly two orange sweets, with the scenario identifiable.
$\frac{672+288+24}{1320}$ [M1]
Guidance: Add the correct exactly-one, exactly-two and exactly-three orange scenarios, including at least one valid three-factor without-replacement product.
$\frac{41}{55}=0.745$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $41/55$ or an accepted decimal; if the method mark is not earned, special-case B1 applies to an accepted final value.
Method 3 — combinations by colour
$\binom41\binom51\binom31+\binom41\binom32+\binom41\binom52+\binom42\binom51+\binom42\binom31+\binom43=164$ [B1]
Guidance: Correctly count the ways for either exactly one orange sweet (112) or exactly two orange sweets (48); unsimplified $\binom41\binom82$ or $\binom42\binom81$ is accepted.
$\frac{164}{\binom{12}3}$ [M1]
Guidance: Add the three correct orange-count scenarios over denominator $\binom{12}3$.
$\frac{41}{55}=0.745$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $41/55$ or an accepted decimal; if the method mark is not earned, special-case B1 applies to an accepted final value.
Method 4 — enumerate by first colour
$P(RRO)+P(ROO)+P(RYO)+P(OOO)+P(YRO)+P(YOO)+P(YYO)$ [B1]
Guidance: Obtain the complete first-colour subtotal $P(R\,\_\,\_)=17/110$ or $P(Y\,\_\,\_)=17/66$; accept an unsimplified equivalent.
$\frac4{55}+\frac1{11}+\frac1{22}+\frac1{3}+\frac1{22}+\frac5{33}+\frac2{33}$ [M1]
Guidance: Add three correct first-colour scenario totals, including at least one valid three-factor without-replacement product.
$\frac{41}{55}=0.745$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $41/55$ or an accepted decimal; if the method mark is not earned, special-case B1 applies to an accepted final value.
Method 5 — first-orange-position complement
$P(O)=\frac4{12},\quad P({-}O)=\frac8{12}\frac4{11},\quad P({-}{-}O)=\frac8{12}\frac7{11}\frac4{10}$ [B1]
Guidance: Obtain $P(\_O)=8/33$ or $P(\_\_O)=28/165$; accept an unsimplified equivalent.
$\frac13+\frac8{33}+\frac{28}{165}$ [M1]
Guidance: Add the three correct first-orange-position scenarios, with at least one valid three-factor product and correct numerator.
$\frac{41}{55}=0.745$ [A1]
Guidance: Award $41/55$ or an accepted decimal; if the method mark is not earned, special-case B1 applies to an accepted final value.
Total: 3
